reason: Full-text proof plan: For odd q≠p, the local cyclotomic Frobenius lemma gives σ_q(ζ)=ζ^q and σ_q(x)≡x^q modulo every prime over q. The Gauss action lemma yields σ_q(τ)=(q/p)τ. Since τ²=p*, one also has τ^q=τ(p*)^{(q−1)/2}≡(p*/q)τ by Euler’s criterion. The image of τ modulo a prime above q is nonzero because q∤p*: otherwise τ²=p* would vanish there. Both signs are ±1 and q is odd, so reduction distinguishes them; equality of the two residues forces (p*/q)=(q/p). This directly proves the restriction action on Q(τ)=Q(√p*) and avoids the generic tower theorem. No earlier quadratic-reciprocity result or geometric Frobenius is used. Sources inspected: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Ch. 6 and Ch. 8 Examples 8.18–8.19; Conrad–Landesman, Math 154 Algebraic Number Theory, Chs. 10–12 and 24; Jerry Shurman, Math 361 Ninth Lecture, §§2–3. Exact dependency IDs and hypotheses examined for the stated finite argument.
